questions.stem: A Linux administrator is deploying a standardized web server configuration across ten servers using Ansible. Arrange the Ansible workflow components and execution steps in the correct order.

options.text: Run ansible-playbook with the --check flag to perform a dry run and validate the playbook.
Review the dry-run output to confirm no unintended changes are planned.
Write the Ansible playbook with hosts, become, and tasks sections targeting the inventory group.
Run ansible-playbook without --check to apply the configuration to all target hosts.
Run "ansible all" with the command module to verify the service is running on all hosts.
Define the target hosts in the Ansible inventory file with appropriate groupings.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Define the target hosts in the Ansible inventory file with appropriate groupings: The inventory file is required before writing the playbook because the playbook's hosts directive references inventory groups. Grouping hosts by role (e.g., webservers) enables selective targeting.
Write the Ansible playbook with hosts, become, and tasks sections targeting the inventory group: The playbook defines the desired state using modules.
Run ansible-playbook with the --check flag to perform a dry run and validate the playbook: The --check flag runs the playbook in dry-run mode, reporting what changes would be made without applying them.
Review the dry-run output to confirm no unintended changes are planned: Reviewing the dry-run output allows the administrator to catch unexpected tasks, such as unintended service restarts or file modifications, before they affect production systems.
Run ansible-playbook without --check to apply the configuration to all target hosts: After the dry run is reviewed and approved, the playbook is executed for real, applying the desired configuration to all ten servers in the inventory group.
Run " ansible all" with the command module to verify the service is running on all hosts: Running an ad hoc command against all hosts confirms that the service is active and running on every target, validating the playbook's outcome.

questions.stem: What signal does pressing Ctrl+D send to the shell?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: EOF

Ctrl+D sends an End-Of-File (EOF) marker, which tells the shell or program that no more input is coming. For example, pressing Ctrl+D at a bash prompt closes the shell session.

SIGTERM is used to gracefully terminate processes.

SIGINT (Ctrl+C) interrupts and terminates foreground processes.

SIGSTOP pauses processes.

questions.stem: Which configuration file defines the DHCP server settings on a Red Hat–based Linux system?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: /etc/ dhcp/ dhcpd.conf

The  /etc/ dhcp/ dhcpd.conf file specifies IP ranges, gateways, and DNS options for dhcpd. For example, defining subnet 192.168.1.0 netmask 255.255.255.0 allocates addresses to clients.

/etc/ dhcp.conf is not a standard file for DHCP. 

/etc/network/interfaces configures network interfaces rather than DHCP settings. 

dhcp.leases stores assigned leases, not the configuration itself.

questions.stem: A user wants to run a script that will modify environment variables within the script but without affecting the system environment variables. What command will let them accomplish this?

The set command is used to display and set names and values of environment variables. The export command is used to make a variable available to child processes. The echo command displays the string that is passed to it as an argument.

questions.stem: After a reboot, the app. service unit did not start. Running systemctl is-failed on another unit listed in the [Unit] section of app. service returns failed. Which directive in app. service MOST likely prevented it from starting?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Requires

The Requires directive sets a unit to start together with the designated units. If any of the designated units do not start, the unit is not started. Because the listed unit reached a failed state, a Requires dependency on it would prevent app. service from starting. The systemctl is-failed command displays failed for any service that has reached a failed state.

The Wants directive also sets a unit to start together with the designated units. However, if those units do not start, the unit is still started.

The Before directive sets the unit to start before the designated units. It controls start order rather than whether the unit starts.

The WantedBy directive is an [Install] section directive that designates which target unit manages the service. It does not list a [Unit] section dependency.

questions.stem: Which component of the Linux boot process is responsible for loading the kernel into memory and starting its execution?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Bootloader

The bootloader is responsible for locating the kernel image on disk, loading it into memory, and starting its execution. It is a crucial step between firmware initialization ( BIOS/ UEFI) and the running kernel. Common bootloaders include GRUB and LILO.

The init system is incorrect because it starts system processes after the kernel has already been loaded. 

Modules are pieces of code loaded after the kernel is running to add functionality such as device drivers.

The BIOS performs the initial hardware checks and hands control to the bootloader, not the kernel directly.

The GRUB configuration file is incorrect because it contains settings used by the bootloader but is not itself responsible for loading the kernel.

questions.stem: A web administrator needs to identify which pages are producing 404 errors on an Apache HTTP Server. Which log file should they review?

httpd.conf is the main configuration file, not a log file.

/var/www/html/logs/server.log is not a standard Apache log location.

questions.stem: Which situation BEST illustrates when to use the sticky bit on a directory?

options.text: When only the system should create new files in that directory
When multiple users share a folder but should only delete their own files
When a directory should deny write access to all users except root
When you want all files in a directory to inherit the same group ownership

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: When multiple users share a folder but should only delete their own files

Setting the sticky bit ( chmod +t) ensures that only file owners or root can remove or rename files within shared directories such as /tmp. This helps to prevent one user from deleting another user's files. 

Denying write access entirely uses permission bits, not the sticky bit.

Group inheritance uses setgid.

System-only write access requires stricter permissions, not the sticky bit.

questions.stem: A web server has been masked for maintenance, and now the administrator wants to restore it and ensure it starts automatically at boot. Which sequence of commands accomplishes this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: systemctl unmask && systemctl enable --now

The systemctl unmask command removes the symbolic link from /dev/null, restoring the service’s ability to be started. The systemctl enable --now command both starts the service immediately and enables it to start automatically at boot, ensuring persistence across reboots.

systemctl reload only reloads configuration for a running service and does not remove a mask or start a stopped unit. systemctl reset-failed clears error states but does not start or enable a service.

systemctl daemon-reload refreshes systemd configuration files but does not start units.

systemctl disable prevents automatic startup at boot, and systemctl restart only restarts an already enabled or unmasked service.

questions.stem:
A web application running on a Linux server returns the following: 403 Forbidden. This happens even though the file permissions and ownership are correct. The service starts normally, and the firewall is configured properly. 

Which issue is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: The network interface is configured without an IPv6 address
The system’s route table does not include a default gateway
The application is using an incorrect DNS resolver
SELinux is enforcing a policy that is blocking access
The system is using an outdated TLS certificate

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: SELinux is enforcing a policy that is blocking access

When SELinux is in enforcing mode, it can prevent services such as web servers from accessing files or directories even when traditional Linux file permissions appear correct. This results in errors like 403 Forbidden despite seemingly proper configuration and can be confirmed by checking audit logs or using commands like getenforce. 

An outdated TLS certificate would cause certificate or browser trust warnings, not an HTTP 403 message.

A missing default gateway affects external connectivity, not local permission access.

Incorrect DNS resolvers can cause name lookup failures. 

Absence of IPv6 does not impact normal IPv4-based local service access.

questions.stem: Which command will configure the disk scheduler to use a single FIFO queue?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: echo noop > /sys/block/sda/queue/scheduler

The noop setting in the scheduler's configuration file will put all I/O requests into a first-in, first-out (FIFO) queue. This is ideal for using less CPU. 

The cfq setting will serve higher priority processes first. The deadline setting will give each I/O request a timer by which they must be completed. There is no setting called fifo.

questions.stem: A technician is diagnosing hardware issues and needs to retrieve detailed information about the system’s processor, manufacturer, and BIOS version directly from the system’s firmware tables. Which command should they use?

dmesg displays kernel messages related to device initialization and does not access firmware data.

lspci lists PCI devices such as network cards or graphics adapters.

lsusb lists USB-connected peripherals. 

ipmitool manages remote hardware monitoring and control.

lscpu summarizes CPU architecture and topology.

Slice units organize and manage resource limits for groups of processes, not task scheduling.

questions.stem: An administrator must ensure that a vulnerable service cannot be started manually with the start command or automatically at system boot. Which systemctl command should the administrator use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: systemctl mask

The systemctl mask command prevents the designated units from starting. A masked service cannot be started using the start command or at system boot because mask links the service to /dev/null. The --now option also immediately stops any running instances, and the systemctl unmask command undoes the effects of mask.

The systemctl disable command marks units not to start automatically at system boot. The service can still be started manually with the start command.

The systemctl stop command stops the designated units. It does not prevent them from being started again.

The systemctl reload command loads a service's modified configuration file without stopping the service. It does not prevent the service from starting.

questions.stem: Which situation is MOST likely to cause high context switching on a Linux system?

options.text: The system is using an outdated TLS cipher suite
The system clock is out of sync with NTP
There are many short-lived processes frequently being created and terminated
A network interface is experiencing packet drops
A process is repeatedly blocked waiting for disk reads

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: There are many short-lived processes frequently being created and terminated

High context switching occurs when the Linux scheduler must frequently switch between large numbers of rapidly starting and stopping processes, causing scheduling overhead and reduced performance.

Blocked disk reads would instead cause high I/O wait.

Packet drops relate to network performance.

NTP clock issues affect time accuracy. 

TLS cipher suite choices impact secure communication, not process switching behavior.

questions.stem: Why is it considered a security best practice to set the default firewall policy to “deny” or “drop” on Linux servers?

It blocks all traffic unless explicitly allowed, minimizing potential attack surfaces
It ensures users can connect from any network

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: It blocks all traffic unless explicitly allowed, minimizing potential attack surfaces

A deny-all (default drop) policy ensures only necessary and explicitly allowed connections are permitted, reducing risk from unknown or unexpected traffic.

Allowing all web traffic would be an unsafe practice.

Performance optimization is not the reason for default deny.

Allowing any network connections without filtering weakens security.

questions.stem: An administrator is ready to make a development app container live. They stop the production app container first, upload the new app container, and then start it up. Which attribute of DevOps are they adhering to in this process?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Replace not update

Rather than updating the app container in production, they are stopping it and replacing it before starting up again. This makes the new container a new environment. 

Version control refers to registering the container and its configuration before moving into production. The static environment refers to a container having libraries and an operating system that cannot change. High availability refers to having replicated app container images in production.

questions.stem: An administrator uses firewall-cmd --add-service= http to open port 80. After a reboot, the change disappears. What must they do to make it persist?

options.text: Use iptables -P ACCEPT to make it persistent
Restart the network manager service twice

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Run firewall-cmd --add-service= http --permanent and reload

firewalld distinguishes between runtime and permanent configurations. Using --permanent saves the rule to disk, and firewall-cmd --reload applies it after reboot. This ensures HTTP remains open across restarts.

Restarting NetworkManager does not persist firewall changes.

/etc/ firewall/active.rules is not used by firewalld.

iptables commands do not affect firewalld’s stored settings.

questions.stem: An administrator wants to see BIOS information from inside Linux. Which command can they run to accomplish this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: dmidecode -t bios

The dmidecode provides information about hardware and requires a DMI/ SMBIOS-compatible computer. The -t option allows for gathering a certain type of information, such as BIOS, memory, or processor. 

The lspci command shows information about PCI buses and devices. The lshw command shows detailed hardware information. The lsdev command gives information on hardware devices. The -t bios option is not applicable to the lspic, lshw, and lsdev commands.

tar.gz and zip are general archive formats and do not provide application portability or isolation.

pkg is a packaging format for macOS, not Linux.

route -n is a legacy command that also displays routing information, but may not show details in newer distributions or with complex setups.

netstat -r prints the kernel routing tables and can also be used to view routes, but may be deprecated in some environments.

lsmod lists kernel modules, not network routes.

questions.stem: Which statement accurately describes a systemd mount unit?

It defines how and where a filesystem is attached to the system
It controls the network routing of mounted drives

Mount units do not handle routing or network paths.

Mount units do not manage file descriptors.

questions.stem: An administrator needs to configure a Linux firewall to translate multiple internal private IP addresses into a single public IP address for outgoing traffic. Which technique should be used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Port Address Translation (PAT)

Port Address Translation (PAT), also known as masquerading, enables multiple internal devices to share a single public IP address by assigning unique source port numbers to each outgoing connection. This technique allows organizations to conserve public IPv4 addresses while still permitting many simultaneous sessions. 

Destination Network Address Translation (DNAT) modifies the destination IP, usually for inbound connections such as port forwarding.

Source Network Address Translation (SNAT) changes the source IP of outbound packets, but it typically maps one private address to one public address rather than handling multiple hosts dynamically.

Static routing defines fixed network paths and does not perform address translation.

Proxy ARP allows a device to respond to ARP requests for another host but has no role in IP address translation.

Reverse DNS resolves IP addresses to hostnames.

rsync can also use SSH for secure transfer, but is primarily designed for efficient directory synchronization and incremental copies.

sftp provides an interactive SSH file transfer session.

wget downloads files from web servers using HTTP, HTTPS, or FTP, but does not use SSH.

questions.stem: What does the chsh command allow a user to do?
questions.explanation:

Primary group changes are done with usermod -g.

Password changes are handled with passwd.

User ID changes are done with usermod -u.

/usr/share/repos/ is not a standard path for repositories.

/var/lib/rpm/ holds RPM database data, not repository configs.

questions.stem: If a process has a PPID of 1, what does this indicate?

options.text: The process is in a zombie state
The process is owned by the kernel only
The process was started directly by the root user
The process has been reparented to init (systemd)

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: The process has been reparented to init (systemd)

PPID refers to Parent Process ID. When a parent process terminates, its child is adopted by PID 1 (init or systemd). This ensures orphaned processes are still managed properly. For example, background daemons often end up with PPID 1 if their original parent exits.

Kernel-only processes do not show up with PPID 1.

Root can start processes, but this does not force PPID = 1.

A zombie is about termination state, not parent assignment.

questions.stem: An administrator creates a public/private key pair with the command ssh-keygen -t rsa. Where will the private key be stored?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: ~/.ssh/id_rsa

A private key will be stored at ~/.ssh/id_rsa. The filename will change depending on the encryption method used. 

The public key will be stored at ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub. The ~/.ssh/authorized_keys file is for logging in without a password. The ~/.ssh/known_hosts file is for storing public keys of servers they have been connected to.

questions.stem: An administrator needs to give read and execute permission to all users for every file and directory inside /public, including subdirectories. Which command should they use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: chmod -R a+rx /public

The chmod -R a+rx /public command recursively (-R) grants read (r) and execute (x) permission to all users (a) for every file and directory under /public. This is required for users to list directory contents ( execute) and view files ( read) across the entire directory tree.

The command chown -R root /public recursively changes ownership to root but does not modify permissions, so it does not ensure access for all users.

The command umask 022 sets the default permissions for new files created, but does not affect permissions for existing files or directories already present in /public.

The command getfacl /public displays the access control list of the directory, but does not change or grant any permissions.

To go down one line, use the enter key. You cannot move the cursor to the right in more. Use the Q key to exit the utility.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of special character devices such as /dev/null?

options.text: They provide a stream interface for certain kernel functions

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: They provide a stream interface for certain kernel functions

Special character devices like /dev/null ( bit bucket) or /dev/zero allow interaction with kernel functions. For example, writing to /dev/null discards data, while reading from /dev/zero produces endless zeros.

They do not represent disk space.

File differences are shown with diff, not special devices.

Inode metadata is accessed via stat, not /dev special files.

questions.stem: A system administrator needs to download a file from a remote web server to the local Linux system using the command line. Which utility should be used for this task?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: wget

wget is a command-line utility designed for non-interactive downloading of files from the web via HTTP, HTTPS, or FTP protocols. It’s particularly useful for downloading large files or entire directories recursively.

curl can download files, but is more often used for interacting with APIs and supports more protocols; it is not as specialized for recursive downloads as wget.

ping tests connectivity, not file transfer.

nc (netcat) is a versatile networking utility, but is not used for web file downloads.

questions.stem: Which setting helps prevent a user from logging in with a password they have used in the past?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Password history

Password history enforces how many previously used passwords a user must avoid before a password can be reused, helping prevent cycling through the same passwords repeatedly. This may increase security protections for an organization. 

Password expiration forces users to change their password after a specific time period.

Password complexity ensures passwords meet criteria such as requiring numbers, symbols, or mixed case.

Password length ensures a minimum number of characters.

Password reuse is the behavior being prevented, not the setting used to enforce the prevention.

questions.stem: What BEST describes a stateful firewall?

options.text: It tracks connection states and allows return traffic for active sessions
It filters traffic based on packet size and header type only
It permits traffic only based on static IP and port rules
It blocks all packets unless rules are manually added for each one

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: It tracks connection states and allows return traffic for active sessions

A stateful firewall keeps a record of active connections and automatically allows legitimate response packets. For example, it lets return traffic from a web request pass without a second rule.

Stateless firewalls rely only on static rules.

Blocking all packets is not a default behavior.

Packet size and headers are not primarily used for filtering in a stateful firewall.

questions.stem: An administrator notices that a Linux production server has unusually high load averages. The "top" command reveals a single process consuming excessive CPU. Arrange the investigation and resolution steps in the correct order.

options.text: Run "pstree -p <PID>" to view the process tree and identify the parent process.
Send "kill -9 <PID> (SIGKILL)" to forcefully end the process.
Run "top" to identify the process with the highest CPU utilization and note its Process Identification Number (PID).
Send "kill -15 <PID> (SIGTERM)" to attempt a graceful termination of the process.
Run "strace -p <PID>" to examine the system calls the suspect process is making.
Run "ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head -10" to confirm the top CPU-consuming processes with full details.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Run "top" to identify the process with the highest CPU utilization and note its Process Identification Number ( PID): This provides a real-time view of process resource usage, allowing the administrator to identify the CPU-heavy process and its PID at a glance.
Run "ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head -10" to confirm the top CPU-consuming processes with full details: Running ps aux with CPU-descending sort provides a static snapshot with full command-line details, confirming the findings from top before taking action.
Run "pstree -p < PID>" to view the process tree and identify the parent process: Understanding the parent-child relationship helps determine whether killing the child process is sufficient or whether the parent process (PPID) must also be addressed to prevent respawning.
Run "strace -p < PID>" to examine the system calls the suspect process is making: The strace command attaches to the running process and reports each system call, providing insight into whether the process is in an infinite loop, waiting on I/O, or exhibiting other abnormal behavior.
Send "kill -15 < PID> (SIGTERM)" to attempt a graceful termination of the process: SIGTERM (signal 15) requests the process to shut down cleanly, allowing it to release resources and write any pending data. This is the preferred first termination attempt.
Send "kill -9 < PID> (SIGKILL)" to forcefully end the process: SIGKILL (signal 9) is used only when SIGTERM does not produce results, as it forces immediate kernel-level termination.

It prevents the file from being modified or deleted

Encryption is handled by other tools such as gpg.

Ownership changes are done with chown.

The immutable setting does not hide files.

questions.stem: What does the output of the diff command represent?

Identical lines are not shown by default.

File type is shown with the file command, not diff.

Binary dumps are not created by diff.

questions.stem: A Linux administrator needs to analyze a large /var/log/syslog file to extract, deduplicate, and count error messages for a report. Arrange the shell pipeline steps in the correct order.

options.text: Run "grep -i 'error' /var/log/syslog" to filter lines containing error messages.
Redirect the final output to errors_summary.txt using > for review.
Pipe the result through "uniq -c" to count and remove duplicate entries.
Pipe the result through "sort" to alphabetically order the extracted values.
Pipe the output through "awk '{print $NF}'" to extract the last field of each matching line.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Run "grep -i 'error' /var/log/syslog" to filter lines containing error messages: First, grep with the -i flag performs a case-insensitive search and passes only matching lines to the next stage of the pipeline.
Pipe the output through "awk '{print $NF}'" to extract the last field of each matching line: Second, awk isolates the last whitespace-delimited field from each line, which typically contains the specific error token or message keyword.
Pipe the result through "sort" to alphabetically order the extracted values: Third, sort orders the extracted fields alphabetically so that identical values are adjacent, which is required for uniq to correctly count duplicates.
Pipe the result through "uniq -c" to count and remove duplicate entries: Fourth, uniq -c collapses consecutive identical lines into a single entry and prefixes each with its occurrence count, producing a frequency summary.
Redirect the final output to errors_summary.txt using > for review: Last, the > redirection operator writes the final counted and deduplicated output to the file errors_summary.txt for reporting purposes.

questions.stem: What is a recommended best practice for Linux service accounts that run background daemons?

Always assign root privileges to simplify management
Assign the minimum privileges necessary and do not use administrative (root) accounts
Share the same account for multiple unrelated services

Giving root access unnecessarily increases risk.

Passwordless logins are insecure and not recommended for service accounts.

Sharing accounts makes auditing and troubleshooting more difficult and increases risk.

questions.stem: A user cannot unmount /mnt/data because it is reported as busy. Which command helps identify the process using that mount point?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: lsof +D /mnt/data

lsof +D lists all open files under a directory, showing which processes are preventing unmounting. For example, if /mnt/data is in use, lsof +D /mnt/data reveals which process is using it, so the admin can stop it safely.

ps -ef | grep data might show processes with data in the name but not which files they are holding open.

htop -p displays details by PID, not by directory.

pidstat -d tracks disk I/O rather than open files.

questions.stem: A new administrator wants every newly created user account to automatically include a .bashrc file in their home directory. Where should this file be placed?

 Files in /etc/skel are copied into the home directory of new users when their accounts are created. This ensures that every new user starts with a consistent environment, such as default shell configuration files (.bashrc, .profile) or custom templates set by administrators. 

/etc/profile sets environment variables. 

/etc/passwd contains user metadata, not files.

/etc/shadow contains password hashes, not templates.

questions.stem: An administrator wants to send remote desktop traffic from local VNC port 5901 through an encrypted Secure Shell (SSH) tunnel to port 5902 on a remote desktop host, starting the tunnel from the client system. Which ssh option establishes this type of port forwarding?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: -L

Local SSH port forwarding sends traffic from the OpenSSH client on the system to the client's OpenSSH server, which forwards it to the destination server through a secured tunnel. It is enacted with the -L option of the ssh command, as in ssh -L 5901:127.0.0.1:5902 -Nf user@example.com. SSH port forwarding, also called SSH tunneling, lets data move through a secure encrypted tunnel similar to a virtual private network (VPN). The AllowTcpForwarding directive in /etc/ssh/sshd_config must be set to yes, which is the default.

The -R option is used for remote SSH port forwarding, which starts at the destination host rather than the client. It is issued on the server, not the client system.

The -X option enables X11 forwarding, which lets a user interact with X11-based graphical utilities on a remote system. It does not forward a specific local port.

The -N option tells OpenSSH that no remote terminal process is desired. It is used alongside a forwarding option but does not establish the forwarding itself.

questions.stem: An administrator edits a DNS zone file and changes an A record. Which command applies the update on a BIND server without restarting the service?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: rndc reload zone_name

rndc reload signals BIND to reload a specific zone after configuration changes, applying updates immediately. For instance, after editing /var/named/example.com.zone, rndc reload example.com applies it live.

Restarting the service disrupts queries temporarily.

dig is simply used to query DNS.

named-checkconf only validates syntax.

questions.stem: Which file descriptor is reserved for the standard output device?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: fd1

Standard output goes to file descriptor 1 and is the device console (/dev/console). It is referred to as stdout. 

Standard input is the console keyboard and is fd0. Standard error is fd2. The bash file descriptor is fd255 and controls terminal information.

questions.stem: Why should organizations use certificates issued by a trusted Certificate Authority (CA) instead of self-signed certificates?

options.text: Self-signed certificates are required for internal private networks
Trusted CA certificates are automatically recognized by browsers and systems, ensuring secure user trust
Trusted CA certificates prevent all types of phishing and spoofing attacks
Trusted CA certificates guarantee the site is safe from malware and phishing attempts

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Trusted CA certificates are automatically recognized by browsers and systems, ensuring secure user trust

Certificates issued by a trusted Certificate Authority (CA) are linked to root certificates already stored in operating systems and browsers, so clients can verify the server’s identity without manual trust steps. This improves user confidence and reduces help-desk issues when accessing internal and external services.

A CA validates identity, not overall site safety and therefore cannot prevent all malware and phishing attacks.  

Encryption strength comes from TLS configuration, not whether a cert is CA-issued or self-signed.

Certificate renewals are required when using trusted CA certificates as well.

Certificate renewals are required when using trusted CA certificates as well.

questions.stem: Which principle of security does allowing users to share accounts violate?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Non-repudiaton

Non-repudiation means that every action can be traced back to an individual. If users share accounts, then it cannot be determined who exactly committed an action. 

Restricting the root account refers to disabling root from terminals and remote access. Separation of data refers to keeping the system partition and log partitions available. Restricting applications refers to jailing them with commands like chroot.

questions.stem: Which directive in a unit file ensures one unit starts only after another unit is started, but does not enforce dependency?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: After

The After directive tells systemd to order the startup sequence so that this unit starts only once the specified unit has started, but it does not prevent this unit from starting if the other unit fails.

The Requires directive enforces a hard dependency; if the required unit fails to start, the dependent unit will also fail to start.

The User directive specifies which account the service should run as, and has nothing to do with the order or dependencies between units.

The Type directive determines how systemd expects the process to behave (such as remaining in the foreground or forking), not the order or dependency between units.

questions.stem: What is the MAIN purpose of a hypervisor?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: To host VMs

Hypervisors, also known as Virtual Machine Monitors (VMM), are used to host Virtual Machines (VMs). VMs are controlled by the hypervisor. The hypervisor provides a virtual environment of CPU time, memory space, and storage space for each VM, but it doesn't store the actual data itself. The primary job of the hypervisor is to host the virtual machines.

questions.stem: Why is Linux designed to separate account information between /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow?

options.text: To reduce disk usage when managing accounts
To improve security by restricting access to hashed passwords
To allow administrators to back up accounts more easily

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: To improve security by restricting access to hashed passwords

Storing only non-sensitive account info in /etc/passwd ( world-readable) while moving password hashes to /etc/shadow ( root-only) improves system security.

This setup does not necessarily make it easier for administrators to back up accounts. 

Disk usage is minimal for these files, so separating them does not provide a disk usage benefit. 

Shell assignment is managed in /etc/passwd, not /etc/shadow. Separating these directories does not simplify shell assignment.

questions.stem: A Linux administrator needs to centralize user authentication across multiple systems so that credentials are stored on a directory server and verified remotely. Which service would be BEST suited for this task?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: LDAP

Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) is used for centralized authentication and directory services, allowing users to use the same credentials across multiple systems by querying a central directory server.

Kerberos provides secure authentication using tickets but relies on a directory or identity service to manage user data.

Samba enables file and print sharing across Windows and Linux systems but is not designed for centralized authentication.

Network File System (NFS) provides network-based file access, not user authentication.

Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) defines how authentication modules interact locally on the host, not across multiple systems.

Secure Shell (SSH) is a secure remote access protocol that authenticates users but does not centralize user databases.

questions.stem: A Linux administrator needs to deploy a Python monitoring script that requires specific library versions not available in the system packages. Arrange the steps to set up and run the script in an isolated Python virtual environment in the correct order.

options.text: Run "python3 -m venv /opt/monitor/venv" to create the virtual environment in the application directory.
Run "pip install -r requirements.txt" to install the required dependencies listed in the project.
Run "source /opt/monitor/venv/bin/activate" to activate the virtual environment in the current shell.
Run "python3 monitor.py" to execute the monitoring script within the isolated environment.
Add the activation and execution commands to a systemd unit file so the virtual environment is used automatically at runtime.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Run "python3 -m venv /opt/monitor/venv" to create the virtual environment in the application directory: First, this creates an isolated Python environment with its own interpreter and pip, preventing dependency conflicts with system packages.
Run "source /opt/monitor/venv/bin/activate" to activate the virtual environment in the current shell: Sourcing the activate script modifies the shell's PATH so that python3 and pip commands reference the virtual environment rather than the system installation.
Run "pip install -r requirements.txt" to install the required dependencies listed in the project: With the virtual environment active, pip installs the exact versions specified in requirements.txt into the isolated environment, not into the system Python.
Run "python3 monitor.py" to execute the monitoring script within the isolated environment: Running the script while the virtual environment is active ensures that all imports resolve to the installed dependencies rather than system packages.
Add the activation and execution commands to a systemd unit file so the virtual environment is used automatically at runtime: Lastly, referencing the virtual environment's Python interpreter directly in the ExecStart directive ensures the correct environment is used when the service is started by systemd.

questions.stem:
A user reports that they cannot write to a mounted data partition. The partition is visible and readable, but touch testfile returns a read-only file system message.

What is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: The partition is out of inodes
The mount point has noexec set
The disk controller firmware needs an update
The user does not own the mount directory
The filesystem was mounted with the ro option

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: The filesystem was mounted with the ro option

Mounting a volume with the read-only (ro) option prevents any write operations and produces the read-only file system error. Remounting with mount -o remount,rw /mountpoint restores write access.

Controller firmware issues cause I/O errors rather than read-only status.

Ownership problems produce a permission denied error, not read-only errors.

Mislabeled SELinux contexts affect access control, not mount attributes.

noexec blocks execution of binaries, not file writes.

inode exhaustion prevents creating new files but allows writes to existing ones.

questions.stem: An administrator needs to add a user alice to the group developers without removing them from existing groups. Which command should they use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: usermod -aG developers alice

usermod -aG adds a user to a supplementary group while keeping their current group memberships. This is important when granting users access to additional resources such as shared project directories or application groups since forgetting the -aG flag would replace all the user’s existing secondary groups and could accidentally remove critical access.

usermod -g changes the primary group and removes all others.

groupmod -a modifies group attributes, not user memberships.

useradd -G is for creating a new user, not modifying an existing one.

optionExplanations.A:

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the line #!/bin/ bash placed at the top of a script?

It does not define environment variables.

The user running the script is determined by permissions, not the shebang.

questions.stem: A system administrator notices that overall CPU usage appears low, but the load average is consistently high. When examining processes, many are marked as D (uninterruptible sleep). Which issue is the MOST likely cause?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: High I/O wait

A high load average with many processes in a D (uninterruptible sleep) state typically indicates that processes are waiting on disk I/O. This means storage performance problems are delaying program execution.

A CPU bottleneck would show high CPU utilization rather than low CPU usage.

A memory leak would result in memory exhaustion and increased swap usage. 

Network jitter affects packet latency, not process scheduling state.

Excessive context switching usually appears as high CPU overhead rather than blocked I/O.

questions.stem: How can an administrator display all Access Control List (ACL) entries for a file called project.txt?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: getfacl project.txt

The getfacl command provides a detailed list of all Access Control List (ACL) entries on the file, showing additional users or groups with access and their permissions, which is essential for troubleshooting or auditing.

chmod +x project.txt adds execute permission to the file but does not reveal ACLs.

passwd project.txt attempts to change the password for a user named project.txt, which does not make sense in this context.

lsmod project.txt lists kernel modules and is unrelated to file permissions.

Slow application response is a symptom, not the underlying cause.

High context switching relates to CPU task scheduling

Packet drops involve network issues, not local disk performance.

ConfigMap supplies configuration data, not replica management.

Service provides network access to pods but does not maintain their counts.

A Secret stores sensitive data such as credentials.

A Volume provides storage but does not manage application high availability.

questions.stem: A process is in a state where it is waiting for a signal from the kernel. What state is it in?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Interruptible sleep

A process that is in the interruptible sleep state is waiting for a signal from the processor. 

A process in the uninterruptible sleep state will wake up from an external event like hardware becoming available. A process in the zombie state has not been acknowledged by its parent process as being killed. A process in the traced, or stopped, state will not have the kernel perform any actions until it is resumed.

questions.stem: An administrator wants to increase the network bandwidth available to a system. What type of bonding should they implement on the network interfaces?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Aggregation

With aggregation, two or more network interfaces can appear as one interface to increase bandwidth. Bonding should first be initialized by adding the module with a command like " modprobe bonding." 

With active/passive, one interface is working while the other is staying idle as a backup. Broadcast is a mode that transmits packets on all interfaces. Load balancing shares the traffic between the network interfaces for redundancy.

questions.stem: In a script, how could you display only the usernames from the first column of /etc/passwd where fields are separated by colons?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: cut -d: -f1 /etc/passwd

The cut command with -d: sets the colon as a field separator, and -f1 extracts the first field, which is typically the username.

head -1 shows only the first line, not the first column.

rm -f would delete the file.

tr ':' '\n' replaces colons with newlines, breaking up the fields, but doesn’t specifically extract usernames.

questions.stem: A Linux administrator notices that a web server process cannot read certain files in /var/www/html, even though file permissions are set correctly. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: The filesystem has run out of inodes
The system’s default gateway is not configured
The SELinux file context for the directory is incorrect
The web server is using an outdated TLS certificate

questions.explanation:
Correct answer:The SELinux file context for the directory is incorrect

In SELinux ( Security-Enhanced Linux), each file and process has a context label that defines what it can access. If the file context does not match the expected label for the service (such as httpd_sys_content_t for Apache), SELinux will block access even if UNIX permissions are correct. Correcting the context with restorecon or chcon restores normal operation. This helps enforce fine-grained access control beyond traditional file permissions.

An outdated TLS certificate affects secure communication, not file access.

A gateway misconfiguration is a network connectivity issue.

Inode exhaustion prevents new file creation but does not cause access denials.

questions.stem: Which symptom is MOST commonly associated with a GRUB misconfiguration on a Linux system?

The system boots directly to a rescue or emergency shell
The system runs out of memory during application execution

Post-login unresponsiveness is more likely related to application or resource issues.

Incorrect mount permissions relate to fstab configuration issues.

Permission denied errors refer to file or directory permission settings.

100–999 are usually reserved for dynamic or service accounts (like daemons).

questions.stem: A Linux administrator wants to view the first ten lines of a large configuration file without opening the entire file in a text editor. Which command should they use?

Grep searches for patterns within text rather than displaying specific line ranges.

Awk is a text processing utility used for pattern scanning and reporting.

questions.stem: An administrator notices that users can access an internal web application using HTTP but not HTTPS. The system uses Uncomplicated FireWall (UFW). Which command should the administrator run to allow secure web traffic?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: ufw allow 443/ tcp

The ufw allow 443/ tcp command opens TCP port 443, which is used by the HTTPS protocol to establish secure, encrypted web sessions. Allowing traffic on port 443 ensures that encrypted communication can reach the web server while still respecting default-deny policies that block other ports.

ufw allow ftp opens port 21 for file transfer, which is unrelated to web access.

ufw allow 22/ tcp enables SSH connections for remote administration but does not affect HTTPS traffic.

ufw enable https is invalid syntax.

ufw allow dns opens port 53, which handles domain name lookups, not secure web traffic.

ufw reload 443 is not valid because reload refreshes all rules but cannot target specific ports.

questions.stem: Which situation MOST clearly indicates the need for a version control system such as Git?

options.text: A project requires converting files from one format to another
Multiple contributors need to make changes to the same files
A project must run on different Linux distributions
A system administrator needs to automate scheduled backups
A user needs to compress files to save disk space

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Multiple contributors need to make changes to the same files 

Version control systems allow multiple contributors to safely modify and track changes to the same files, preventing accidental overwrites and reducing coordination errors.

File format conversion does not require version control.

Backups and scheduling are handled by tools such as cron or backup utilities, not Git.

questions.stem: A Linux administrator is troubleshooting an SELinux access denial and wants to analyze the audit logs to identify which rule caused the violation and what corrective action SELinux recommends. Which tool should be used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: sealert

The sealert utility, part of the SELinux Troubleshooting ( setroubleshoot) package, analyzes SELinux audit logs located in /var/log/audit/audit.log and provides human-readable explanations for denials. It identifies which domain or context caused the issue and often suggests corrective actions such as enabling a boolean, restoring a file context, or adjusting a policy. 

getsebool displays or modifies the current values of SELinux booleans.

audit2allow converts audit messages into custom SELinux policy modules that permit the denied actions, but it does not explain why the denials occurred.

restorecon resets file context labels to their default values.

setenforce changes SELinux modes between Enforcing and Permissive, which affects enforcement but provides no diagnostic data.

ausearch can query audit logs directly, but it returns raw log entries that require manual interpretation and do not include recommendations.

questions.stem: A developer has completed work on a feature branch and now needs to combine those changes into the main branch while maintaining a clean project history. Which Git command should they use to integrate the feature branch?
questions.explanation:

git rebase also combines branches but rewrites commit history, which can lead to conflicts if used on shared branches.

git push uploads local commits to a remote repository but doesn’t merge branches.

git reset modifies the current head or undoes commits without combining branches.

git checkout switches branches or restores files.

git stash temporarily saves uncommitted work but does not integrate branches.

questions.stem: A standard user needs to run several administrative commands as root. The user must authenticate with their own password, and the root account's login shell script must run so its environment variables are set. Which command should the user run?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: sudo -i

The sudo command allows a standard user account to run commands as another user account, including root, and prompts the user for their own password to validate who they are. Adding -i lets the user become the other user and run that account's login shell script to set its environment variables. The /etc/sudoers file defines which users and groups, such as the wheel or sudo group, are allowed to use sudo.

The su - command also runs the substitute user's login shell script. However, the su command requires the password for the substitute user account rather than the user's own password.

The sudoedit command opens a file in a text editor with another user's privileges. It does not provide a login shell for running several commands.

The visudo command securely opens the sudoers file in an editor so changes can be made safely. It does not run commands as root.

questions.stem: After a server reboot, a critical database service ( postgresql) fails to reach the active (running) state. Arrange the troubleshooting steps in the correct order.

options.text: Run "journalctl -u postgresql -xe" to review detailed journal entries for the failure.
Run "systemctl restart postgresql" and confirm resolution with systemctl status.
Run "systemctl daemon-reload" to apply any changes made to the unit file.
Run "systemctl status postgresql" to view the service state and recent log output.
Identify and correct the misconfiguration in the unit file or the service's own configuration.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Run "systemctl status postgresql" to view the service state and recent log output: This provides an immediate summary of the service state, the last few log lines, and the exit code, giving the administrator the initial clues needed for diagnosis.
Run "journalctl -u postgresql -xe" to review detailed journal entries for the failure: This filters journal output to the postgresql unit, while -x adds explanatory catalog text and -e jumps to the end of the log, surfacing the specific error that caused the failure.
Identify and correct the misconfiguration in the unit file or the service's own configuration: After reviewing the logs, the administrator can determine whether the failure is due to a missing file, an incorrect path in the unit file, a port conflict, or a database configuration error and make the appropriate correction.
Run "systemctl daemon-reload" to apply any changes made to the unit file: If the unit file was modified, daemon-reload must be run to inform systemd of the changes before restarting the service.
Run "systemctl restart postgresql" and confirm resolution with systemctl status: Restarting the service applies the corrected configuration, and immediately checking status confirms the service has transitioned to the active (running) state.

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY benefit of setting the setgid bit on a directory used by a project team?

options.text: Only the directory owner can create files in the directory
The directory cannot be deleted by any user
New files inherit the group ownership of the directory
All files in the directory are encrypted automatically

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: New files inherit the group ownership of the directory

Setting the setgid (set group ID) bit on a directory ensures that any files or subdirectories created inside will automatically have the group ownership of the parent directory. This is especially useful for project or departmental folders, as it ensures group members retain access regardless of who creates the file.

Only the directory owner can create files in the directory if permissions are set restrictively, but the setgid bit itself does not limit file creation; it manages group ownership.

The setgid bit does not perform any encryption; encryption must be configured separately.

The ability to delete the directory depends on parent directory permissions and whether the directory is empty, not the presence of the setgid bit.

questions.stem:
A system administrator needs to copy all files from /var/log to /mnt/backup while preserving timestamps, permissions, and directory structure. They also want to copy only files that have changed since the last backup. 

Which tool should they use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: rsync

rsync is ideal for synchronizing directories and performing incremental backups because it copies only changed files while preserving timestamps, permissions, and ownership. It is commonly used for backups over both local and networked systems.

dd performs block-level copying of devices or partitions, not file-based incremental backups.

cp copies files but lacks incremental and metadata-preserving capabilities.

tar creates full archives each time rather than synchronizing changed files.

gzip compresses individual files.

cpio can archive and copy files but is less efficient for incremental or network-based backups.

questions.stem: An administrator is using Docker Swarm to orchestrate containers running on several separate physical servers. In Docker Swarm, what is each physical server called?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Node

Docker Swarm is Docker's orchestration system for managing containers running on separate physical servers, and each physical server is called a node. Swarm can monitor the cluster's health and return the cluster to the desired state if a container fails. It can also deploy additional Docker containers if the desired app performance is not being met.

In Docker Swarm, as in Docker Compose, application containers are called services. A service is not a physical server.

A cluster is a group of Docker containers that appears to a user as a single container. It is not an individual physical server.

A pod is a Kubernetes component that contains one or more running containers. It is not a Docker Swarm term for a physical server.

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of IMAP4 in email systems?

options.text: To download and delete messages from the server immediately
To access and manage email messages while keeping them on the server

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: To access and manage email messages while keeping them on the server

Internet Message Access Protocol version 4 ( IMAP4) allows users to access, organize, and manage emails on a remote mail server without downloading or deleting them by default. This enables synchronization between multiple devices, so changes like moving or reading emails are reflected everywhere. 

SMTP handles sending messages.

POP3 typically downloads and removes messages from the server.

A third-party tool would likely be needed to compress attachments. IMAP does not handle attachment compression.

questions.stem: A system administrator updates the configuration for the SSH service and needs the changes to take effect immediately. Which action should they perform with systemctl?

systemctl mask blocks the service from starting, which is not desired here.

systemctl status only displays information about the service and does not reload or restart it.

questions.stem: A DevOps team wants an open source automation utility that is managed by the Linux Foundation and was forked from HashiCorp's commercial Terraform utility. Which utility should the team choose?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: OpenTofu

OpenTofu is managed by the Linux Foundation and is a fork of the commercial Terraform automation utility by HashiCorp. It uses the standard JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) data format to define server configuration data. Automation utilities such as OpenTofu support automated configuration management so production app containers can be replicated without manual configuration.

SaltStack is a Python-based configuration management tool owned by VMware. It stores server configuration data in YAML ( YAML Ain't Markup Language) data structures.

Chef is a Ruby-based package that uses Ruby-based recipes to define server configurations. It can run in either a client-server mode or a stand-alone mode.

Puppet uses its own language to define system configurations for remote servers. It uses a client-server architecture that requires remotely controlled servers to run a client application.

questions.stem: An administrator notices that an account has a UID of 1050. What does this indicate?

options.text: The account is reserved for root-only services
The account will expire after 30 days by default
The account is a regular user account
The account is a predefined system account

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: The account is a regular user account

UIDs starting at 1000 and above are reserved for regular user accounts in most modern Linux distributions. A UID of 1050 indicates a standard human-created login account.

Predefined system accounts typically have UIDs below 100 (and sometimes up to 999 depending on distro).

UID 0 is the root account. Root-only services do not use 1050.

Expiration is controlled by /etc/shadow settings and chage, not the UID.

questions.stem: Where do most Debian-based Linux systems store their local time zone setting?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: /etc/timezone

The time zone for most Debian-based systems is defined in the /etc/timezone file. The file is not in a text format, so it can't be edited directly to change the time zone. Rather, you need to link that file to a template file stored in the usr/share/zoneinfo folder. 

The /etc/localtime file is for Red Hat-based systems. The /etc/local.conf file has system locale and keyboard map settings. The /etc/bashrc file is for setting and configuring the bash shell.

questions.stem: Which type of DNS record is used by mail servers to identify where email for a domain should be delivered?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: MX record

A Mail eXchange (MX) record directs email to the correct mail server for a domain by mapping the domain name to a mail host’s Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN). This allows other servers to locate where messages should be delivered, often using a priority value to decide which server to try first.

An A record maps a hostname directly to an IP address. This is unrelated to mail exhange. 

A Canonical NAME (CNAME) record is a DNS record that links one domain name to another.

TXT records hold text-based information and often store security information such as SPF or DKIM data.

passwd -e forces password reset, not expiration.

usermod -d changes the home directory.

questions.stem: A Linux administrator wants to view the date and time when each user last successfully logged into the system. Which command provides this information?

who shows currently logged-in users, not historical logins.

id displays the current user’s UID, GID, and group memberships.

getent passwd lists user account entries from /etc/passwd but does not include login timestamps.

groups shows a user’s group memberships only.

finger can display user details like name and home directory but not last successful login times.

questions.stem: A Linux administrator must back up the /etc directory, compress the archive, transfer it to a remote system, and then restore a single configuration file from the backup. Arrange the backup and restore steps in the correct order.

options.text: Run "tar -tzf /tmp/etc_backup.tar.gz" to verify the archive contents before transfer.
Use "rsync -avz /tmp/etc_backup.tar.gz user@remote:/backups/" to transfer the archive.
Run "tar -czf /tmp/etc_backup.tar.gz /etc" to create a compressed archive of /etc.
Run "tar -xzf /backups/etc_backup.tar.gz etc/ssh/sshd_config" to extract the specific file.
Copy the extracted sshd_config to the correct location and reload the SSH daemon.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Run " tar -czf /tmp/etc_backup. tar.gz /etc" to create a compressed archive of /etc: First, tar with the czf flags creates (c) a gzip-compressed (z) archive file (f) of the /etc directory in a single command.
Run " tar -tzf /tmp/etc_backup. tar.gz" to verify the archive contents before transfer: The t flag lists the archive contents without extracting, allowing the administrator to confirm the backup is complete and uncorrupted before sending it off-site.
Use " rsync -avz /tmp/etc_backup. tar.gz user@remote:/backups/" to transfer the archive: Then rsync with -avz transfers the archive over Secure Shell (SSH) with archive mode, verbose output, and compression, ensuring an efficient and verified transfer.
Run " tar -xzf /backups/etc_backup. tar.gz etc/ssh/ sshd_config" to extract the specific file: Supplying a path argument to tar xzf extracts only the specified file from the archive rather than expanding all contents, which is the correct selective restore technique.
Copy the extracted sshd_config to the correct location and reload the SSH daemon: After extraction, the file must be placed at /etc/ssh/ sshd_config and the SSH daemon must be reloaded so the restored configuration takes effect.

questions.stem: What is the MAIN purpose of using a cryptographic hash function when storing passwords on a Linux system?

options.text: To compress the password for storage
To encrypt files for network transmission
To store a one-way, irreversible representation of the password for secure verification
To allow users to view each other’s passwords

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: To store a one-way, irreversible representation of the password for secure verification

Hash functions create a fixed-size output that cannot be reversed to obtain the original password, so even if the hash is stolen, the password itself remains protected.

Hashes are not used to encrypt files; encryption is a separate process.

Compression reduces data size but does not secure or hide password values.

Hashes are specifically designed to prevent users from seeing each other’s passwords.

questions.stem: A Linux administrator wants to prevent users from reusing the same password repeatedly to improve account security. Which PAM module setting would BEST enforce this control?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: pam_pwhistory

The pam_pwhistory module keeps a record of previously used passwords and prevents users from reusing them within a defined history depth. This ensures password history and reuse policies are enforced consistently across accounts.

pam_tally2 tracks failed authentication attempts and can lock an account after a threshold is reached.

pam_faillock is a newer alternative to pam_tally2 that also manages failed login attempts rather than password reuse.

pam_pwquality enforces password complexity requirements such as length and character variety but does not prevent reuse.

pam_unix provides basic authentication against the system’s shadow password file and lacks history enforcement.

pam_loginuid sets and maintains a login UID for auditing sessions.

questions.stem: A system administrator needs to check the current system time settings and verify whether NTP time synchronization is enabled. Which command should they use?
questions.explanation:

The sysctl time suggestion does not display system time information; sysctl is used to adjust kernel parameters.

The systemd-analyze time command does not exist. systemd-analyze is primarily used for measuring boot performance.

The resolvectl status command provides DNS resolution details handled through systemd-resolved.

The systemctl list- timers command lists scheduled timers configured under systemd but does not provide time synchronization or clock configuration information.

questions.stem: An administrator pauses a foreground job in the terminal using Ctrl+Z. What state does the process enter?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Stopped

Ctrl+Z sends the SIGTSTP signal, which places the process into the stopped state, meaning it is paused but not terminated. For example, pausing a text editor mid-session suspends the process until it is resumed with fg.

Running means it is still actively using the CPU.

Sleeping means it is waiting on a resource, not manually paused.

A zombie is a terminated process awaiting cleanup.

questions.stem:

data_link pointing to /var/data/file1.txt
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: ln -s /var/data/file1.txt data_link

The ln -s option creates a symbolic link, with the target first (/var/data/file1.txt) and link name second (data_link). Symbolic links act like shortcuts, pointing to another location in the filesystem without duplicating data. For example, an administrator might use ln -s /var/data/file1.txt ~/data_link so that a user can quickly access a deeply nested file from their home directory.

ln /var/data/file1.txt data_link creates a hard link rather than a symbolic link.

ln data_link /var/data/file1.txt reverses the order, which is incorrect.

ln -s data_link /var/data/file1.txt is also in incorrect order.

questions.stem: A user has two jobs suspended in the background. They type fg %2. What happens?

options.text: The job with PID 2 is resumed in the foreground
The second job is resumed in the foreground

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: The second job is resumed in the foreground

The fg command brings a specific job, referenced by its job number (like %2), into the foreground. For example, if vim is job 2 in the background, running fg %2 reopens vim in the current shell.

To terminate background jobs, you would use kill %job_number (e.g., kill %2) or kill PID if you know the process ID. You could also use killall process_name or pkill pattern for broader matches.

PIDs and job numbers are different. %2 means job number 2, not PID 2.

The shell is not terminated by fg. There are numerous ways to terminate the shell, such as pressing exit or pressing Ctrl+D to send EOF at the prompt.

questions.stem: A Linux administrator needs to encrypt a new data partition /dev/sdb1 using Linux Unified Key Setup 2 (LUKS2) with the Argon2 key derivation function and configure it to mount persistently at /mnt/secure. Arrange the encryption and mount configuration steps in the correct order.

options.text: Add the mapping entry to /etc/crypttab for automatic unlock at boot and the filesystem entry to /etc/fstab to mount the partition automatically after unlock.
Run "cryptsetup luksFormat --type luks2 --pbkdf argon2id /dev/sdb1" to format the partition with LUKS2 encryption.
Run "cryptsetup luksOpen /dev/sdb1 secure_data" to open and map the encrypted partition.
Mount /dev/mapper/secure_data to /mnt/secure and verify read/write access.
Run "mkfs.ext4 /dev/mapper/secure_data" to create a filesystem on the decrypted device mapper.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Run " cryptsetup luksFormat --type luks2 --pbkdf argon2id /dev/sdb1" to format the partition with LUKS2 encryption: First, luksFormat writes the LUKS2 header and sets the key derivation function to Argon2id, which provides strong resistance against brute-force attacks.
Run " cryptsetup luksOpen /dev/sdb1 secure_data" to open and map the encrypted partition: Second, luksOpen unlocks the encrypted partition using the passphrase and creates a transparent device mapper entry at /dev/mapper/secure_data, which can be used like a standard block device.
Run " mkfs.ext4 /dev/mapper/secure_data" to create a filesystem on the decrypted device mapper: The filesystem is created on the mapped (decrypted) device, not on the raw /dev/sdb1. 
Mount /dev/mapper/secure_data to /mnt/secure and verify read/write access: The mounted filesystem is tested to confirm successful encryption and access.
Add the mapping entry to /etc/crypttab for automatic unlock at boot and the filesystem entry to /etc/fstab to mount the partition automatically after unlock: Last, /etc/crypttab defines the mapping name, the source device, and the key file (or "none" for passphrase prompt), instructing the system to unlock the partition during boot.

questions.stem: What information is stored in the /etc/group file?

options.text: Password hashes, account expiration and group membership
Groups, their GIDs, and group members

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Groups, their GIDs, and group members

/etc/group defines groups, their numeric IDs (GIDs), and lists the members. This file is essential for managing permissions since group membership determines access to shared resources such as project directories or application files. For example, adding a developer to the docker group via /etc/group allows them to run Docker commands without needing root privileges.

/etc/shadow contains password hashes and expiration.

/etc/passwd holds login shell and home directory.

Kernel parameters are not stored in /etc/group.

questions.stem: Which command enables and starts the Apache HTTP Server on a system using systemd?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: systemctl enable --now httpd

The command systemctl enable --now httpd activates the Apache HTTP Server immediately and configures it to start automatically when the system boots. This ensures that websites hosted on the server remain available even after reboots or maintenance cycles. An administrator might use this command on a Red Hat–based server after installing Apache to bring a new site online without manually starting the service each time.

service apache2 is used on Debian-based systems and references a differently named service, not compatible with Red Hat’s naming convention.

apachectl restart simply restarts Apache but does not configure it to start automatically on boot.

systemctl start nginx controls the Nginx web server, which is a completely different application from Apache.

questions.stem: A server’s web application crashes because the system reports “No space left on device,” but df -h shows plenty of free disk space. What is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: The web application’s process was killed by the Out of Memory (OOM) killer
The system’s RAM is fully utilized
The filesystem has run out of available inodes

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: The filesystem has run out of available inodes

When df -h shows free space but files cannot be created, it usually means the filesystem is out of inodes, which are metadata structures used to track files. Each file and directory consumes an inode, so even if there is physical space left on the disk, no new files can be created once all inodes are used.

Full RAM affects memory availability, not storage.

A swap partition misconfiguration impacts virtual memory, not file creation.

An Out of Memory (OOM)  killer termination affects processes, not disk space usage.

questions.stem: A Linux administrator needs to configure a static IP address on a server using NetworkManager. The interface is ens33 and should use IP 192.168.1.50/24 with gateway 192.168.1.1. Arrange the nmcli configuration steps in the correct order.

options.text: Run "nmcli con up static-ens33" to activate the connection profile on the interface.
Run "nmcli con add type ethernet ifname ens33 con-name static-ens33" to create the connection profile.
Run "nmcli con mod static-ens33 ipv4.addresses 192.168.1.50/24" to assign the static IP address.
Run "nmcli con mod static-ens33 ipv4.gateway 192.168.1.1 ipv4.method manual" to set the gateway and disable Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP).
Run "ip address show ens33" to verify the static IP address is correctly assigned.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Run " nmcli con add type ethernet ifname ens33 con-name static- ens33" to create the connection profile: First, nmcli con add creates a new NetworkManager connection profile named static- ens33 that is bound to the ens33 interface.
Run " nmcli con mod static- ens33 ipv4.addresses 192.168.1.50/24" to assign the static IP address: Second, nmcli con mod sets the desired static IP address and prefix length on the newly created profile.
Run " nmcli con mod static- ens33 ipv4. gateway 192.168.1.1 ipv4.method manual" to set the gateway and disable Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP): Setting ipv4.method to manual disables DHCP and configures the default gateway. Both changes must be made before activating the connection.
Run " nmcli con up static- ens33" to activate the connection profile on the interface: Then nmcli con up applies the profile to the interface, replacing any existing connection and assigning the static IP address.
Run "ip address show ens33" to verify the static IP address is correctly assigned: Finally, ip address show confirms that the interface has the correct IP address and prefix and is in the UP state.

questions.stem: Which command provides a secure way to overwrite and destroy data before file deletion?

rm only removes the filename from the directory index.

truncate changes the file size. 

mv simply relocates a file to a different directory rather than destroying it.

GPG encrypts individual files and emails, not entire storage devices.

SHA-256 is a hashing algorithm used for integrity verification.

WireGuard encrypts network traffic in transit, not data stored on disk.

ls -l only lists directory contents, not open processes.

find is used to locate files. 

stat shows metadata for specific files.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: ip link show

The ip link show command displays interface details, including the assigned MAC address, allowing administrators to verify whether it matches the expected hardware address. Detecting unexpected changes can indicate MAC spoofing or tampering.

ip addr flush dev eth0 removes IP configuration rather than inspecting it.

arp -n lists neighbor MAC addresses but not the local interface address.

ethtool -i eth0 shows driver information, not MAC address spoofing evidence.

ss -tuln lists listening sockets and open ports.

dig -x performs reverse DNS lookups, which is unrelated to hardware address verification.

questions.stem: An administrator wants to automate server configuration across many remote servers without installing a separate agent software package on each remote server. Which tool BEST meets this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Ansible

Ansible, owned by Red Hat, has the main selling point that remotely controlled servers do not need to run a separate agent software package. It uses OpenSSH and Python to communicate with remote servers and uses a text-based playbook to define the tasks to execute for an inventory of hosts. Ansible is an example of an orchestration engine that provides agentless orchestration.

Puppet uses a client-server architecture. It requires remotely controlled servers to run a client application in the background.

In Kubernetes, each worker is a pod host system that uses a kubelet ( agent) to communicate with cluster services.

Docker Compose defines multiple containers and their shared resources in a single YAML ( YAML Ain't Markup Language) file. It runs and manages those containers only on the same physical server.

questions.stem: A Linux server cannot resolve external hostnames even though internal IP connectivity is confirmed working. Arrange the Domain Name System (DNS) troubleshooting steps in the correct order.

options.text: Run "systemctl status systemd-resolved" to check whether the local DNS resolver is running.
Run "cat /etc/resolv.conf" to verify the nameserver entries are correctly configured and "cat /etc/nsswitch.conf" to confirm DNS is listed in the hosts: line after files.
Run "dig google.com" to test DNS resolution and note the server address and response status.
Correct the misconfigured resolver entry and run "resolvectl status" to confirm resolution works.
Run "ping 8.8.8.8" to confirm basic IP connectivity to external networks is functioning.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Run " ping 8.8.8.8" to confirm basic IP connectivity to external networks is functioning: First, pinging an external IP address isolates the problem to DNS rather than routing.
Run " dig google.com" to test DNS resolution and note the server address and response status: Then dig provides detailed DNS query information, including which nameserver was queried, the response code, and the answer section, pinpointing where resolution fails.
Run " cat /etc/resolv.conf" to verify the nameserver entries are correctly configured and " cat /etc/nsswitch.conf" to confirm DNS is listed in the hosts: line after files: Next, /etc/resolv.conf specifies the nameserver IP addresses used for resolution, and /etc/nsswitch.conf controls the order in which name resolution methods are tried.
Run " systemctl status systemd-resolved" to check whether the local DNS resolver is running: On systems using systemd-resolved, the local stub resolver at 127.0.0.53 must be active.
Correct the misconfigured resolver entry and run " resolvectl status" to confirm resolution works: Lastly, after the misconfiguration has been identified and fixed, this confirms whether queries are resolving successfully.
